sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Name the three gunas.
Name the five koshas.
questions.answer: Annamaya, Pranamaya, Manomaya, Vijnanamaya and Anandamaya.

questions.q: Give the meaning of 'persona'.
questions.answer: A mask worn by actors in Greek and Roman theatres, the source of the word personality.

questions.q: Give the signs of healthy Annamaya Kosha.
Name the five Pranas.
questions.answer: Prana, Apana, Samana, Vyana and Udana.

questions.q: What is the Anandamaya Kosha made of?
questions.answer: Vasanas (desires) in the subconscious, giving peace and bliss.

questions.q: How can Manomaya Kosha be developed?
questions.answer: By studying good literature such as poems, novels and essays, and by prayer and resolutions.

questions.q: What is the Psychic being according to Sri Aurobindo?
questions.answer: The innermost core of the being, a spark of the Divine, also called Atman.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Tamas should be maximised. (ii) Everyone is a combination of the three gunas.
questions.answer: (i) False – kept to a minimum. (ii) True.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the guna: (i) moderate and meditative; (ii) restless and work-addicted; (iii) idle and lethargic; (iv) which should be kept minimum?
Match the Prana: (i) perception; (ii) excretion; (iii) circulation; (iv) thinking.
Name the kosha: (i) food sheath; (ii) vital sheath; (iii) sheath of bliss; (iv) intellectual sheath.
Name the activity for each kosha: (i) asanas; (ii) breathing exercises; (iii) reading literature; (iv) identifying with all fellow beings.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why is personality not just physical appearance in the Indian view?
questions.answer: It extends to physical, social and spiritual levels, with the Atman as its core.

questions.q: Describe a Sattwik person.
questions.answer: Moderate in habits, meditates, works as worship, loves and helps others and radiates knowledge.

questions.q: What is the Annamaya Kosha?
questions.answer: The physical body, the outermost food sheath formed from food and returning to food.

questions.q: What does the Pranamaya Kosha regulate?
questions.answer: It regulates the food sheath through the five Pranas that support bodily functions.

questions.q: Differentiate mind and intellect.
questions.answer: Mind receives stimuli and stores memories and emotions; the intellect discriminates, judges and takes rational decisions.

questions.q: Why is Anandamaya Kosha called blissful?
questions.answer: Because, as in deep sleep, it brings undisturbed peace with the cessation of agitation.

questions.q: What is the vertical system of Sri Aurobindo?
questions.answer: A staircase of planes of consciousness from the inconscient to the highest Sat-Chit-Ananda.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the Indian concept of personality.
questions.answer: Personality is the whole of existence – physical, social and spiritual – with the Atman as its core, not merely external appearance.

questions.q: Describe the three gunas and the three types of persons.
questions.answer: Sattwa is light (meditative, loving), Rajas is dynamism (active, restless) and Tamas is inertia (idle, lethargic). Everyone has all three; development keeps Tamas minimum.

questions.q: Describe the Pranamaya Kosha.
questions.answer: The vital sheath comprising the five Pranas for perception, excretion, digestion, circulation and thinking; it regulates the body, and its healthy development shows in enthusiasm, discipline and honesty.

questions.q: Distinguish Manomaya and Vijnanamaya Koshas.
questions.answer: Manomaya is the mental sheath of feelings, emotions and memories; Vijnanamaya is the intellectual sheath of imagination, knowledge, insight and discriminating decisions.

questions.q: How can the Annamaya and Pranamaya Koshas be developed?
questions.answer: Annamaya by regular, right food, exercise, games and asanas; Pranamaya by pranayama and breathing exercises.

questions.q: Explain Sri Aurobindo's concentric system.
questions.answer: A series of rings: outer awareness of physical, vital and mental sheaths; inner mind in touch with universal mind; the innermost Psychic being or Atman, a spark of the Divine.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any one kosha in detail.
questions.answer: Annamaya Kosha, the food sheath, is the physical body formed from the essence of food; it exists by food and goes back to food. With proper exercise and diet it develops; signs are fitness, agility, stamina, endurance, motor skills and eye–hand coordination, and it is the instrument of worship.

questions.q: Describe the ways for development of the five koshas.
questions.answer: Annamaya: right food, exercise, asanas; Pranamaya: pranayama; Manomaya: good literature, prayer; Vijnanamaya: debates, problem solving, small research, interviewing eminent people; Anandamaya: identifying with fellow beings and the universe.

questions.q: Explain the theory of trigunas and the right proportion for personality development.
questions.answer: Sattwa (light), Rajas (dynamism), Tamas (inertia) combine in everyone. Sattwik people are calm, Rajasik restless and active, Tamasik idle. Development moves from Tamas to Rajas to Sattwa and beyond; Rajas is needed somewhat, Tamas minimal.

questions.q: Describe the Panch Koshas and Sri Aurobindo's levels of consciousness.
questions.answer: Five sheaths: annamaya, pranamaya, manomaya, vijnanamaya, anandamaya, with Atman distinct. Sri Aurobindo's concentric rings lead to the Psychic being, and the vertical system rises from the inconscient to Sat-Chit-Ananda.
